Busca is a variation of CiapanÃ² (also known as Rovescino, Traversone, or Tressette a non Prendere), a reverse trick-taking game from Lombardy, Italy. CiapanÃ² was very popular in Lombardy until the 1980s and is still played there.
40-card pack: Italian suits (swords, batons, cups, coins) or Milanese/French suits (spades, clubs, hearts, diamonds). Cards rank: 3 (high), 2, Ace, King, Horse/Queen, Jack/Fante, 7, 6, 5, 4 (low).
40-card Italian or Milanese pack, score sheet for tracking busche
Deal 10 cards to each player (anticlockwise). Turn to deal passes to the right after each hand.

items.text: CiapanÃ² target score variants: Some groups play CiapanÃ² with a target score of 21 or 41 instead of 31, changing when players are eliminated or the match ends.
Lowest-score-wins ending: Some play that when a player reaches or exceeds the target score, the player with the lowest cumulative penalty score immediately wins.
Ace-of-clubs 21-point variant: A Traversone variant in which the Ace of clubs is worth 11 points and there are 21 total points in each deal, with cappotto allowing a large score swing.
Kifameno (Who Wins Least): Kifameno is a Slovenian losing Tressette variant where 2–4 players are dealt 10 cards each and undealt cards form a draw stack that is used between tricks.
